name: Archaeological Site of Mystras
description: Mystras is a ruined medieval hill town in the Peloponnese, Greece, climbing the slopes of the Taygetus mountains above the plains of ancient Sparta. A Frankish prince began it with a fortress in 1249, and it later became the Byzantine capital of the Morea, home to scholars and artists. Visitors wander empty palaces, churches and lanes until the town's abandonment in the 1830s.
